answers.text:
Dear Mr Ellery,

I write you this letter for informing you about a work in my house, because it can be a little problem for you also.

Firstly, the roof of my house is very old and in the winter the water come inside from two place. So the workers will change all the tile and they will put a new isolation under it. The work start in 12 May and it take almost two week, every day from eight in the morning to five in the evening.

Secondly, there will be a noise of course, but it is only a normal noise of a work and I think you not hear it too much in the day time.

Thirdly, the workers must to use the path in the side of your house, because in my side there is no place for the ladder and the machine. They will pass with the materials from there in the morning and in the evening, this is the only solution for us.

I will be in the home in this period, so if there is a problem you can knock my door in any time.

Best wishes,

Selin Kaya

why_this_band.task_response: The work and the dates are given concretely, and the request for access is made too; but the second point drops to a single sentence, and that sentence downplays the impact instead of describing it (only a normal noise, you not hear it too much). Phrasing the request directly with must to use breaks the register in a letter to a neighbour.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Firstly / Secondly / Thirdly are mechanically laid over the three points, and the second paragraph finishes in a single sentence. The work–impact–request order is still logical, though, and the reader does not lose what is being asked.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Vocabulary is everyday and repetitive: work, problem, noise keep recurring, and isolation is a wrong choice for insulation. The only phrase belonging to a letter is I am sorry for this situation; there is nothing to soften the request.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Almost every sentence has an error: I write you, for informing, the water come, from two place, all the tile, start in 12 May, it take, two week, you not hear, must to use, in the side, in the home, knock my door in any time. Structures are simple sentences and short reasons added with so / because.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Write the second point without downplaying it: honestly describe which days the noise will peak, the dust, and the closed passage. Using a request pattern such as I would be very grateful if you could allow instead of must to use would also settle the register.

answers.text:
Dear Mr Ellery,

I am writing to let you know about some repair work on my roof next month, and to ask you a small favour.

The tiles above the back bedroom have been leaking from the storm in February, so that side of the roof has to be stripped and laid again. The builders will start on Monday 12 May and they expect to finish in about ten working days. They have promised me to not use the noisy machine before nine in the morning.

I am afraid the work will be unpleasant for you as well. There will be a lot of hammering in the first three days, and some dust will certainly come in your garden. The scaffolding will also take a part of the light from your kitchen window for two week.

My favour is about the path on the side of your house. The builders cannot reach the roof from my garden because of the old plum tree, so they need to carry the ladders through your path, perhaps four times in a day. There would be only two men and they have agreed to clean the path every evening.

Please tell me if this is not convenient and I will ask them to find another way. My phone number is on the back of this letter, so you can call me if the noise become a problem.

Kind regards,

Selin Kaya

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are addressed: the work and its duration are given with dates, its effect on the neighbour is described in a separate paragraph through noise, dust and light, and the request is made along with its scope. How long it would last if the request is granted is clear, but exactly what will be cleaned up at the end of the work stays a little general.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Paragraphs are logically split and each carries a single point. Links are provided through familiar patterns such as I am afraid / My favour is about; transitions are accurate but flat.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: Items suited to the task, such as stripped, scaffolding, hammering, convenient, favour, are present, and the request is politely worded. In places such as laid again, take a part of the light, the collocation does not quite settle.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: Relative clauses, the passive and the conditional pattern are correctly formed, and long sentences do not fall apart. About half the sentences have a preposition, plural or agreement error (leaking from the storm, to not use, the noisy machine, come in your garden, for two week, through your path, in a day, the noise become); meaning is never blocked.

answers.what_would_lift_it: Most errors cluster in prepositions and singular/plural; a read-through before sending that checks only these (for two weeks, in a day, the noise becomes) would move the grammar up one band.

answers.text:
Dear Mr Ellery,

I am writing to warn you about some work due to start on my roof next month, and to ask a favour of you at the same time.

The tiles above the back bedroom have been letting water in since the February storms, and the roofer says patching is no longer worth doing, so the rear slope will be stripped and relaid. The men are booked for Monday 12 May and reckon on ten working days, weather permitting. They will work from eight until five, with the noisier tools kept back until after nine.

I am sorry to say that you will hear a good deal of it. The first three days, when the old tiles come off, will be the worst, and there is bound to be dust in your garden. The scaffolding will stand against the gable and may take some of the light from your kitchen window, although it should be down again by the end of the fortnight.

The favour is this. The old plum tree makes it impossible to bring a ladder up my own side, so the roofer has asked whether his men might use the path along the side of your house. It would be two of them carrying materials, perhaps four times a day, and they have agreed to sweep the path each evening and make good any damage.

Do say if this would be a nuisance and I will ask them to find another way round. My number is on the back of this letter, in case the noise becomes too much.

Kind regards,

Selin Kaya

why_this_band.task_response: All three points are complete and balanced: what the work is and why it cannot be postponed, its effect on the neighbour day by day, and the request with how many people, how many times, and what would happen afterwards. The offer to withdraw if it causes a problem and the phone number make the request acceptable.
why_this_band.coherence_cohesion: Five paragraphs carry the letter's logic, and a short return such as The favour is this marks the shift. Time and place information arrives exactly when the reader needs it, and no paragraph drifts to a second topic.
why_this_band.lexical_resource: There are less common items suited to letter register: weather permitting, bound to be, make good any damage, a nuisance, the end of the fortnight, the rear slope. The second paragraph gets briefly dense with technical detail.
why_this_band.grammatical_range_accuracy: The use of tenses and conditional structures is flexible and accurate; error-free sentences are close to all of them. The second sentence of the third paragraph reads breathlessly because it carries three pieces of information at once.

answers.what_would_lift_it: The word warn in the opening is too harsh for a letter of favour; let you know or give you some warning would be more suitable. Splitting the long sentence in the third paragraph in two would also ease the rhythm.
